title: Possessive Articles in Accusative
sourceNote: The transcript is badly garbled. The rule and the table are clear; the example sentences are reconstructed from context, and the exercise sentences are rebuilt in standard German.
objectives: I can use mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer in the accusative
I can add -en to the possessive article for masculine objects
I can talk about my family with accusative sentences
I can pick the right possessive form in a sentence

patterns.form: Subject + verb + possessive article + masculine noun (-en).
Subject + verb + possessive article + feminine / neuter / plural noun (no change).

grammar.title: The rule: masculine gets -en
grammar.body:
Possessive articles (*mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr/Ihr*) work like *ein* and *kein*. In the accusative only the **masculine singular** changes: add **-en**.

*Das ist mein Vater.* (nominative) – *Ich liebe meinen Vater.* (accusative).

For feminine, neuter and plural nouns nothing changes: *meine Mutter, mein Auto, meine Eltern*.
grammar.ar: مع المذكر المفرد نضيف en فقط. أما المؤنث والمحايد والجمع فلا تتغير.

grammar.title: Table: possessive articles in the accusative
grammar.body: Note the spelling of **unser** and **euer**: *unser → unseren*, *euer → euren* (the *e* before *r* drops out). Also: *eure* (feminine / plural) but *euren* (masculine).

grammar.title: More sentences
grammar.body: Always look at the **noun** (the object), not at the owner, to decide whether to add -en. The owner only decides *which* possessive word (mein, dein, sein ...).

mistakes.why: *Vater* is a masculine accusative object: add *-en*.

lines.en: Are you visiting your uncle today?

lines.de: Ja, und ich besuche auch meine Tante.
lines.en: Yes, and I am also visiting my aunt.

lines.de: Nein, aber ich kenne deine Schwester.
lines.en: No, but I know your sister.

tip: Check the gender of the noun first. If it is *der*, add *-en* to the possessive article.

comprehension.q: Which nouns change their possessive article in the accusative?
What is the accusative of 'mein' with 'Vater'?
What happens to 'unser' and 'euer' in the masculine accusative?
Does 'meine Mutter' change in the accusative?

exercises.title: Fill in the possessive article
exercises.instructions: Write the correct accusative form of the word in brackets.

items.a: Sie besucht ihren Großvater. / Sie besucht ihren Opa.

exercises.title: Put the words in order
exercises.instructions: Form a correct sentence. Both word orders are accepted.

items.a: Ich besuche meinen Onkel. / Meinen Onkel besuche ich.
Er kennt unseren Vater. / Unseren Vater kennt er.
Er liebt seine Mutter. / Seine Mutter liebt er.
Ich kenne deine Schwester. / Deine Schwester kenne ich.

summary: Possessive articles work like ein and kein.
Only masculine singular objects get -en: mein → meinen, dein → deinen, sein → seinen, ihr → ihren.
Feminine, neuter and plural objects keep the nominative form: meine Mutter, mein Auto, meine Eltern.
